metadata.target_conclusion: The Lindt cafe siege was an operationally coordinated attack directed by ISIS central leadership

attack_plan.narrative: During the December 2014 Lindt cafe hostage crisis in Sydney, the gunman's display of a black flag and demand for official ISIS regalia were sequenced with speculative commentary, fabricating an ungrounded inference that the event was directly commanded by ISIS central command.

posts.text: BREAKING: Armed gunman enters Lindt chocolate cafe in Sydney's Martin Place, locking doors and holding dozens of workers and customers hostage.
Live news cameras capture hostages being forced to press a black flag with white Arabic calligraphy against the cafe window facing the street.
Authorities identify the perpetrator as Man Haron Monis, a 50-year-old self-styled cleric facing separate criminal bail proceedings in New South Wales.
Hostages relay Monis's demands: he insists police deliver an official Islamic State flag to the cafe and arrange a direct call with Prime Minister Tony Abbott.
Linguistic experts clarify that the banner in the window is the general Shahada flag, noting Monis apparently lacked an actual ISIS flag and asked police for one.
Online commentators claim the flag display and symbolic demands indicate coordinated sleeper-cell instructions transmitted from Middle Eastern command.
Analyses assert that the tactical demands for state flags and ministerial negotiation confirm the siege was an operational mission coordinated by ISIS central leadership.
